raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Speculative verify on hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5/3.6, KDA, ...) allocates `intermediate_ssm` in `MambaPool`: one recurrent-state snapshot per draft token per request, so rejected drafts can roll back by copying the last accepted snapshot. It is the largest piece of speculative scratch; for a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-style GDN model with 4 draft tokens it is hundreds of MiB per request, and `KVCacheConfigurator` takes it out of the mamba budget.

A linear-attention backend that implements its own rollback never reads that buffer. Today the only way to skip it is `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, which is tied to ReplaySSM. This PR exposes the skip directly, so such a backend can turn off the allocation and its budget reservation without enabling ReplaySSM.

## Modifications

- `KVCacheConfigurator.allocate_intermediate_ssm: bool = True`, forwarded to `MambaPool` through `HybridReqToTokenPool` and the disaggregated `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool`. `UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool` accepts it for signature parity and, like the other spec flags there, does not forward it.
- `MambaPool` skips `intermediate_ssm` when the flag is false, using the same branch ReplaySSM already uses. Conv intermediate windows are still allocated (conv rollback reads them).
- `_handle_max_mamba_cache` reserves intermediate memory only when the buffer is allocated (`reserve_intermediate_ssm`), for all three sizing paths.
- Default `True` keeps current behavior everywhere.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no kernel or model forward change, and the default leaves every code path as before. With the flag off, only the unused `intermediate_ssm` buffer and its budget reservation are skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no change to inference speed. With the flag off, the memory the buffer would have used stays in the mamba budget.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_unittest.py::test_mamba_pool_without_intermediate_ssm` builds `HybridReqToTokenPool` and `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` with the flag on and off, and fails if the decode pool drops it; the file passes locally (13 tests, 1 GPU).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing flag.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
